wages.text: Kounalakis said that strong unions are foundational to the middle class and a thriving California.
wages.quote: hard work, opportunity, and strong unions are the foundation of the middle class and of a thriving California.

housing.text: Kounalakis said she would accelerate housing construction and supported legislation streamlining housing development and expanding housing opportunities.
housing.quote: we must dramatically increase housing production across all income levels, especially near jobs and transit

sentencing.text: Kounalakis co-sponsored legislation that increased penalties for sex-trafficking offenders.
sentencing.quote: enhances California’s ability to combat sex trafficking by increasing penalties for offenders and expanding critical services for survivors.

immigration.text: She praised the benefits of generous immigration policies and called for ending the treatment of immigrants and their families that she described as terrible.
immigration.quote: California has benefited from America’s generous immigration policies over the last few generations in particular.

abortion.text: Kounalakis co-sponsored legislation to protect access to abortion medication and providers and patients from out-of-state prosecution.
abortion.quote: to ensure continued access to abortion medication in California and protect providers and patients from out-of-state interference.

energy.text: Kounalakis finalized a settlement to shut down an offshore oil platform and described her infrastructure plans as working toward California’s climate goals.
energy.quote: Finalized a settlement to shut down Platform Esther, reducing California’s offshore oil platforms to just two active sites

housing.text: Hawks supports directing housing funding toward producing more housing units and tying homelessness-program funding to measurable reductions.
housing.quote: Calls for housing dollars to produce actual units, supports housing-finance metrics tying funding to homes, and supports tying homelessness programs to reductions.
